comment: Student plan going up a dollar hurts when I'm already broke. Still paying for now but I'm going to check the student rate on Apple Music before the next billing date.
Paying $12.99 and still no lossless is a joke. Tidal has had HiFi for years. Cancelled Spotify and moved everything over today.
Family plan went up $2 for six accounts, and split five ways it's still pretty cheap. Not a big deal to me.
I hope the extra money actually reaches artists. Spotify has said that before. I'll believe it when per-stream payouts change.
Third price hike in a few years while the app keeps filling up with podcasts and video. This is pure greed. Canceling.
Everything has gone up. A dollar more a month isn't going to make or break me, so I'm staying.
Duo going up $2 stings a bit, but it's still cheaper than two individual plans, so we're staying put.
I already pay for YouTube Premium, which includes YouTube Music. Not paying Spotify more when I can just switch.
Honestly the hike is fine. I'm mostly here for the podcasts and audiobooks, and I'd pay for those anyway.
Going back to the free tier with ads. I'm not paying more for something I used to get for free.
Apple Music is already cheaper and I'm in the Apple ecosystem anyway. Switching this month.
People complaining about a dollar need to remember Spotify has been losing money for years. The old price was too low.
I can't justify it anymore. I'm dropping Spotify entirely and using library apps and free radio.
Amazon Music Unlimited is cheaper through Prime, and I already pay for Prime. Moving over.
Didn't even notice until the email came in. Whatever.
Ugh, $12.99. Still no lossless, still no real upgrades to the app, and I'm still paying. Annoying, but I'm staying.
As an independent artist I'd love this to translate into better payouts. Probably won't, but I'm not going to fight it.
This is the last straw. Cancelled and telling my friends to leave too. Their profits keep going up and the product keeps getting worse.
A dollar more to keep Spotify running is worth it for me. Totally fine with it.
Tidal has lossless and didn't raise its price the same way. I'm out of Spotify and the lossless gap was the final reason.
Honestly I'd just download stuff at this point. Not paying more for a worse app.
We're downgrading from Duo to Individual. $18.99 isn't worth it when we barely overlap in what we listen to.
The Family price bump means we're dropping to Duo now that the kids are older and don't need their own accounts.
The student plan still beats everything else. Six ninety-nine is a steal, so I'm paying it without complaint.
I expected it honestly. Netflix, Disney and everyone else went up, so Spotify waited long enough.
The price is fine with me. The app is what bugs me. The redesign made searching worse and I still have to pay for it.
Deezer has a cheaper plan with hi-fi included. Switching this week.
The price went up, the playlists are still there, and I'm not going to think about it again.
